heroData.title: EOR in Kenya
heroData.subtitle: Hire in Nairobi
heroData.description: Compliant employment in East Africa's hub. We handle SHIF, NSSF, and the Housing Levy.

steps.title: KRA PIN Acquisition
steps.description: Obtain Kenya Revenue Authority Personal Identification Number (PIN) for the employee. This is mandatory for all tax filings and statutory deductions.

steps.title: NSSF & SHIF Registration
steps.description: Register the employee with the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) and the new Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF), which replaced NHIF in October 2024. This ensures access to social security and health benefits.

steps.title: Housing Levy Setup
steps.description: Configure payroll to deduct the mandatory Affordable Housing Levy (1.5% from employee, 1.5% from employer) as per the 2024 regulations.

steps.title: Employment Contract Issuance
steps.description: Issue a compliant employment contract outlining terms, salary in KES, working hours (max 52/week), and leave entitlements under the Employment Act 2007.

steps.title: Bank Account Details
steps.description: Collect local bank account details or mobile money (M-Pesa) information for salary disbursement. M-Pesa is widely accepted for salary payments.

rows.label: Management Fee
values: Monthly fee per employee. Varies by volume and complexity.

rows.label: NSSF (Tier 1)
values: Capped at KES 480 (Employer) and KES 480 (Employee) for earnings up to KES 8,000.

rows.label: NSSF (Tier 2)
values: Capped at KES 3,840 (Employer) and KES 3,840 (Employee) for earnings between KES 8,000 and KES 72,000.

rows.label: Housing Levy
values: Mandatory affordable housing levy on gross salary.

rows.label: SHIF (Health)
values: Employer must remit but does not match. Deducted from employee gross.

rows.label: NITA
values: Monthly Industrial Training Levy per employee.

items.title: Strict Termination Laws
items.text: Termination in Kenya is procedurally strict. Employers must provide valid reasons and hold a disciplinary hearing where the employee can bring a representative. Unfair termination can lead to damages of up to 12 months' pay.

items.title: Contracts Required
items.text: Written contracts are mandatory for any employment exceeding 3 months. They must specify job description, hours, leave entitlement, and termination notice.

items.title: Immigrant Quotas
items.text: EORs cannot automatically hire foreigners. The entity must have available 'immigrant quotas' or process a Class D work permit, which is costly and scrutinized.

questions.question: Can I hire foreign nationals using an EOR in Kenya?
questions.answer: Yes, but it requires a Class D Work Permit. The EOR provider must sponsor the permit, which adds cost (approx. KES 500,000/year) and time (2-4 months) to the process.

questions.question: What is the notice period for resignation?
questions.answer: Typically one month, or payment in lieu of notice. During probation (usually 3-6 months), the notice period is often 7 days.

questions.question: Is probation mandatory?
questions.answer: No, but it is standard practice. The maximum probation period is 6 months, extended to 12 months in some cases with employee consent.

steps.title: Data Collection
steps.description: Gather attendance data, overtime hours (1.5x weekdays, 2.0x weekends/holidays), and any bonuses or allowances by the 20th of the month.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Calculate PAYE tax, NSSF, SHIF, and Housing Levy. Apply Personal Relief (KES 2,400/month) to reduce tax liability.

steps.title: Payment Disbursement
steps.description: Transfer net salaries to employee bank accounts or M-Pesa wallets. Typically done by the 25th-30th of the month.

steps.title: Payslip Distribution
steps.description: Issue secured digital payslips to employees detailing all earnings and statutory deductions.

steps.title: Statutory Remittance
steps.description: File returns and remit payments to KRA (PAYE, Housing Levy), NSSF, and SHA by the 9th of the following month to avoid penalties.

items.title: M-Pesa Integration
items.text: Mobile money (M-Pesa) is a valid and popular method for salary payments in Kenya. Ensure integration with bulk payment systems (B2C) for efficiency.

items.title: Housing Levy
items.text: The 1.5% Housing Levy is mandatory for all employees, including expatriates, and is calculated on gross salary. It is not a benefit but a tax.

items.title: Personal Relief
items.text: Every resident employee is entitled to a Personal Relief of KES 2,400 per month, which is directly deducted from the PAYE tax payable.

questions.question: Is there a mandatory 13th-month pay?
questions.answer: No, a 13th-month bonus is not legally required in Kenya. However, performance bonuses are common and taxable.

questions.question: Are allowances taxable?
questions.answer: Yes, cash allowances (housing, transport, utilities) are generally added to gross income and taxed. Some non-cash benefits may be taxed as 'Benfits in Kind'.

questions.question: What is the penalty for late PAYE remittance?
questions.answer: Late filing attracts a penalty of KES 10,000 or 25% of tax due (whichever is higher). Late payment attracts 5% penalty plus 1% monthly interest.

items.title: NITA
items.description: 9th of the following month (often paid annually or semi-annually by compliance).

steps.title: Gross Salary
steps.description: Start with monthly gross income.

steps.title: Allowable Deductions
steps.description: Deduct NSSF (Tier 1 & 2 only) contribution to get 'Taxable Income'. Housing Levy and SHIF are NO LONGER deductible before tax (check latest finance act as this fluatuates, currently treated as post-tax or separate levy).

steps.title: Calculate PAYE
steps.description: Apply the graduated tax bands (10% to 35%) on the Taxable Income.

steps.title: Less Relief
steps.description: Subtract Personal Relief (KES 2,400) from the PAYE figure. Any insurance relief (15% of premiums) is also subtracted here.

steps.title: Other Deductions
steps.description: Deduct Housing Levy (1.5% of Gross) and SHIF (2.75% of Gross).

steps.title: Net Pay
steps.description: Gross - (PAYE after relief + NSSF + SHIF + Housing Levy).

items.title: Reliefs
items.text: Personal Relief is KES 2,400 per month. Insurance relief is 15% of premiums paid, capped at KES 5,000 per month.

items.title: Levies on Gross
items.text: Remember: Housing Levy and SHIF are calculated on the GROSS salary, not the taxable salary.

questions.question: Are bonuses taxed?
questions.answer: Yes, bonuses are added to gross income and taxed at the marginal PAYE rate.

questions.question: How is overtime taxed?
questions.answer: Overtime is fully taxable as income.

heroData.title: Incorporation Kenya
heroData.subtitle: eCitizen Portal
heroData.description: Register a Private Limited Company (Ltd) via the digital eCitizen platform.

steps.title: Account Creation
steps.description: Create an eCitizen account. Foreign directors can do this using a foreigner certificate or visitor visa details.

steps.title: Name Search & Reservation
steps.description: Perform a name search on the Business Registration Service (BRS) portal. Reserve the approved name (valid for 30 days).

steps.title: Form CR1 & CR2
steps.description: Complete Form CR1 (Application for Registration) and CR2 (Model Memorandum for a Private Company limited by shares).

steps.title: Director Details & BOI
steps.description: Provide details for Form CR8 (Notice of Residential Address/Director particulars) and the Beneficial Ownership Information (BOI) register.

steps.title: Payment & Certificate
steps.description: Pay the registration fee (approx. KES 10,650). Upon approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation and CR12 (Official Search).

rows.label: Registration Fee
values: Standard fee for Private Ltd Company.

rows.label: Legal/Agency Fees
values: If using a Company Secretary or Lawyer.

rows.label: Business Permit
values: Nairobi City County Single Business Permit (varies by office size).

rows.label: KRA Returns (Nil/Active)
values: Monthly VAT & Annual Corp Tax filing.

items.title: Passport/ID
items.description: Copies of ID (Citizens) or Passport bio page (Foreigners) for all directors/shareholders.

items.title: Passport Photos
items.description: Recent colored passport-sized photos for all directors.

items.title: KRA PIN
items.description: Personal KRA PIN for all Kenyan directors. Foreigners must obtain individual KRA PINs.

items.title: Registered Address
items.description: Physical address in Kenya (LR Number, Building, Street).

questions.question: Can a foreigner fully own a company in Kenya?
questions.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is permitted for most sectors. Some sectors like insurance, telecommunications, and aviation may have local equity participation requirements.

questions.question: Do I need a resident director?
questions.answer: No, a resident director is not legally mandatory for private limited companies, but having a local representative can ease bank account opening and tax registration.

questions.question: How long does incorporation take?
questions.answer: With eCitizen, the process is streamlined and can often be completed in 3-7 working days, provided all systems are functioning and documents are correct.

items.title: KCB (Kenya Commercial Bank)
items.description: Largest bank network, robust regional presence.

items.title: NCBA
items.description: Strong corporate banking and asset finance.

heroData.title: Staffing in Kenya
heroData.subtitle: Silicon Savannah
heroData.description: Hiring top tech and business talent in Nairobi. From developers to sales execs.

rows.label: Recruitment Fee
values: Of annual gross salary. Retainer may apply.

rows.label: Work Permit (Class D)
values: Annual issuance fee. Processing fee: KES 20,000 (Non-refundable).

steps.title: Briefing & Role Definition
steps.description: Define the JD, budget, and hybrid/remote requirements. Nairobi talent is competitive.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Utilize LinkedIn, BrighterMonday, and local tech communities (e.g., Moringa School alumni).

steps.title: Screening & Assessment
steps.description: Technical assessments for devs (HackerRank, etc.) and soft-skill interviews.

steps.title: Background Checks
steps.description: Verify academic certificates, credit reference bureau (CRB) status, and certificate of good conduct (DCI) if sensitive role.

steps.title: Offer & Contract
steps.description: Extend offer letter ensuring it aligns with Kenyan labour laws (salary in KES, benefits).

items.title: Silicon Savannah
items.text: Nairobi is a major tech hub. Talent is proficient in JavaScript, Python, Java, and mobile dev (Android/Flutter).

items.title: Universities
items.text: Top talent often comes from University of Nairobi, Strathmore University, and JKUAT.

items.title: Counter-Offers
items.text: The senior developer market is tight. Be prepared for counter-offers from big players like Microsoft, Google, and Visa who have local hubs.

questions.question: Can I background check criminal records?
questions.answer: Yes, candidates can provide a 'Certificate of Good Conduct' from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI).

questions.question: What is the typical notice period?
questions.answer: Usually 1 month. For very senior roles, it can be negotiated to 2 or 3 months in the contract.

questions.question: Do I need to pay a 13th-month salary?
questions.answer: It is not mandatory by law, but performance bonuses are a common retention tool.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.description: Primary source for professional and tech talent.

heroData.title: HRIS Kenya
heroData.subtitle: KRA Integrated
heroData.description: HR systems complying with iTax, SHIF, and NSSF reporting standards.

items.title: FaidiHR
items.description: Local cloud-based HR/Payroll specializing in Kenyan statutory compliance (iTax, NSSF, SHIF).

items.title: Workpay
items.description: Pan-African HR/Payroll platform with strong Kenyan roots and time-tracking features.

items.title: Sage 300 People
items.description: Robust enterprise solution widely used by larger corporations in Keyna.

steps.title: iTax P10 CSV
steps.description: System must generate the specific P10 return CSV format required for upload to the KRA iTax portal.

steps.title: Statutory Logic Updates
steps.description: Ability to quickly update logic for changing rates (e.g., recent SHIF 2.75% and Housing Levy 1.5%).

steps.title: Leave Management
steps.description: Track statutory leave (21 days annual, sick leave, maternity/paternity) to ensure compliance.

steps.title: ESS Portal
steps.description: Employee Self Service for accessing payslips, P9 forms (tax cards), and applying for leave.

items.title: P9 Forms
items.text: Kenyans need P9 tax cards at the end of the year to file their individual returns. Your HRIS must generate these automatically.

items.title: Data Protection
items.text: Ensure the provider complies with the Kenya Data Protection Act, 2019. Data residency options within Kenya are a plus.

questions.question: Can I use a global HRIS?
questions.answer: Yes, but global tools often struggle with the specific CSV formats for KRA iTax and NSSF. You may need a local middleware or payroll partner.

questions.question: Is cloud HRIS accepted?
questions.answer: Yes, cloud adoption is high. Just ensure data privacy compliance.

heroData.title: Accounting Kenya
heroData.subtitle: IFRS Standards
heroData.description: Bookkeeping, audit, and tax compliance adhering to IFRS and Companies Act 2015.

items.title: IFRS
items.text: Kenya fully adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). SMEs can use IFRS for SMEs.

items.title: ICPAK
items.text: The Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Kenya (ICPAK) regulates the profession. Ensure your accountant is a member in good standing.

steps.title: Bookkeeping
steps.description: Maintain daily records of sales, purchases, and expenses. VAT invoices must be ETR (Electronic Tax Register) compliant via eTIMS.

steps.title: Financial Stmts
steps.description: Prepare annual financial statements (Balance Sheet, P&L, Cash Flow) within 6 months of year-end.

steps.title: Statutory Audit
steps.description: Audit is mandatory for companies, though some small companies may be exempt if they meet specific turnover/asset criteria (consult a local expert).

steps.title: Tax Returns
steps.description: File Corp Tax return (IT2C) on iTax by end of 6th month after year-end.

steps.title: Annual Return
steps.description: File Annual Return with Registrar of Companies via eCitizen to update company details.

rows.label: Monthly Retainer
values: For bookkeeping, payroll, and VAT returns for small entities.

rows.label: Annual Audit
values: Varies significantly by turnover and complexity.

rows.label: Tax Consulting
values: For robust tax planning and transfer pricing.

items.title: eTIMS
items.description: Electronic Tax Invoice Management System. Mandatory for all businesses to generate valid tax invoices.

items.title: iTax
items.description: KRA's online portal for all tax filing and payments.

items.title: eCitizen
items.description: Portal for Registrar of Companies filings (Annual Returns).

questions.question: What is eTIMS?
questions.answer: It is KRA's system for electronic invoicing. Every business transaction must be supported by an eTIMS invoice to be deductible for tax purposes.

questions.question: When is the corporate tax deadline?
questions.answer: The return must be filed and tax paid by the last day of the 6th month following the end of the financial year (e.g., June 30th for Dec 31st year-end).

items.title: Unfair Termination
items.description: Courts are pro-employee. Failure to follow due process (hearings, notices) will result in huge compensation awards.

items.title: Data Protection
items.description: The Data Protection Act 2019 enforces strict handling of personal data. Employers need to be registered as Data Controllers/Processors.

items.title: Sexual Harassment
items.description: Employers with 20+ employees must have a sexual harassment policy statement.

steps.title: Valid Reason
steps.description: Identify a fair reason (misconduct, poor performance, physical incapacity, or redundancy). Structure the allegations clearly.

steps.title: Show Cause Letter
steps.description: Issue a 'Show Cause' letter detailing the allegations and inviting the employee to explain their defense in writing.

steps.title: Disciplinary Hearing
steps.description: Hold a formal hearing. The employee MUST be allowed to bring a colleague or union rep. Minutes must be taken and signed.

steps.title: Notice of Termination
steps.description: If the outcome is dismissal, issue a termination letter. Pay salary in lieu of notice if immediate exit is required.

steps.title: Certificate of Service
steps.description: Legally required document stating employment dates and role. Do not include negative remarks unless requested by the employee.

steps.title: Terminal Dues Payment
steps.description: Pay all accrued salary, leave days not taken, and gratuity (if in contract) within the statutory timeline (usually immediate or next payroll).

steps.title: Contracts
steps.description: Verify all staff have signed contracts compliant with Employment Act.

steps.title: WIBA Policy
steps.description: Ensure Work Injury Benefits Act (WIBA) insurance is active for all employees.

steps.title: Statutory Receipts
steps.description: Keep proof of remittance for NSSF, SHIF, Housing Levy, and PAYE for 7 years.

steps.title: Safety Registration
steps.description: Workplace must be registered with DOSHS (Director of Occupational Safety and Health Services).

items.title: ODPC
items.description: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner.

questions.question: Is WIBA mandatory?
questions.answer: Yes, every employer must have an insurance policy to cover liability for workplace injuries.

questions.question: Can I hold employee passports?
questions.answer: No, it is illegal to confiscate personal documents like passports or IDs.

items.title: Trade Unions
items.text: Employees have a constitutional right to join unions. Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBAs) can supersede individual contracts.

rows.label: VAT
values: Standard rate. 8% for fuel. 0% for exports.

rows.label: Digital Service Tax (DST)
values: On gross transaction value for digital services (non-residents).

rows.label: Management / Professional Fees
values: High impact on cross-border service charges.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Ensure tax obligation is added to your KRA PIN on iTax (Income Tax, VAT, PAYE).

steps.title: Monthly VAT
steps.description: File VAT returns by the 20th of the following month. Nil returns must be filed if no trading occurred.

steps.title: Installment Tax
steps.description: Pay estimated CIT in 4 installments (20th of 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months).

steps.title: Final Return
steps.description: File final Self Assessment Return (IT2C) by end of 6th month after year-end and pay balance.

items.title: EPZ & SEZ
items.text: Export Processing Zones (EPZ) enjoy a 10-year corporate tax holiday. Special Economic Zones (SEZ) have reduced rates (10% for first 10 years).

items.title: Minimum Tax
items.text: Minimum tax provisions have faced legal battles. Always check current status with a tax advisor as this area is litigious.

items.title: Foreign Tax Credits
items.text: Kenya allows deduction of foreign tax paid on foreign income, restricted to the tax that would have been payable in Kenya.

questions.question: What is the VAT threshold?
questions.answer: Annual turnover of KES 5 Million. Voluntary registration is possible.

questions.question: Does Kenya have Double Tax Treaties?
questions.answer: Yes, with UK, Canada, France, India, Sweden, Germany, and others. This can reduce withholding tax rates.

items.title: June 30
items.description: Deadline for Individual Income Tax returns (for year ending Dec 31).

heroData.title: Legal Kenya
heroData.subtitle: Common Law
heroData.description: Legal frameworks based on English Common Law.

items.title: English Common Law
items.text: Kenya's legal system is based on English Common Law, making it familiar to investors from UK, US, and Commonwealth jurisdictions.

items.title: Dispute Resolution
items.text: Nairobi Centre for International Arbitration (NCIA) is gaining traction, but litigation can be slow. Arbitration clauses are highly recommended.

steps.title: Governing Law
steps.description: Explicitly state 'Laws of Kenya'.

steps.title: Dispute Clause
steps.description: Specify arbitration place and language (English).

steps.title: Currency
steps.description: Clarify payment currency to manage forex risk.

rows.label: Contract Review
values: Flat fee per document often possible.

questions.question: Are digital signatures valid?
questions.answer: Yes, recognized under the Business Laws (Amendment) Act and Electronic Transactions reporting.

questions.question: Can we use foreign law contracts?
questions.answer: Yes for B2B, but employment contracts for work in Kenya generally must adhere to mandatory provisions of Kenyan law.

heroData.title: Software Kenya
heroData.subtitle: Mobile First
heroData.description: The home of M-Pesa. Strong fintech and mobile development ecosystem.

items.title: Mobile Money
items.text: M-Pesa API integration is virtually mandatory for B2C apps. It processes more volume than cards.

items.title: Connectivity
items.text: 4G is widespread, 5G is rolling out. Smartphone penetration is high, but consider data-light apps for mass market.

steps.title: Define Stack
steps.description: JS/TS, Python, and Java (Android) are very popular.

steps.title: Test Locally
steps.description: Use practical tests. Internet stability is generally good for remote work.

steps.title: Equip
steps.description: Provide a good laptop (MacBooks are prized but expensive locally). Data allowance is a common perk.

points.title: Copyright Automatic
points.description: Software code is protected as a literary work under the Copyright Act immediately upon creation.

points.title: KECOBO Registration
points.description: Voluntary registration with the Kenya Copyright Board (KECOBO) is recommended for easier enforcement.

points.title: Silicon Savannah
points.description: Nairobi is the epicenter, hosting major global tech HQs (Google, Microsoft, Visa).

points.title: Konza Technopolis
points.description: An upcoming key smart city project aimed at driving BPO and ITO services.

items.title: Cloud
items.description: AWS and Azure have strong local communities. Local data centers exist (e.g., IXafrica).

questions.question: Is IP protected?
questions.answer: Copyright Act exists, but enforcement can be tricky. Contracts should be water-tight on IP assignment.

questions.question: Are there tech hubs?
questions.answer: Yes, iHub, Nairobi Garage, and others foster a vibrant community.

heroData.title: Marketing Kenya
heroData.subtitle: Digital & Social
heroData.description: Engaging 'KOT' (Kenyans on Twitter) and utilizing TikTok for youth reach.

items.title: KOT (Kenyans on Twitter)
items.text: X (Twitter) is powerful. 'KOT' can make or break brands virally. Tone deafness is severely punished.

items.title: Influencers
items.text: Micro-influencers often deliver better ROI than celebs. TikTok is exploding for under-30 demographic.

steps.title: Localize Content
steps.description: Use 'Sheng' (slang) appropriately if targeting youth. Generic English ads can perform poorly.

steps.title: Select Channels
steps.description: Facebook (Mass Market), Instagram (Lifestyle), TikTok (Gen Z), LinkedIn (B2B).

steps.title: Engage
steps.description: Community management is key. Respond quickly to comments.

items.title: Digital consultancies
items.description: Many boutique firms like Squad, Bean Interactive, etc.

questions.question: Is radio relevant?
questions.answer: Yes, vernacular radio is huge for reaching rural populations.

questions.question: What about TV?
questions.answer: Still dominant for mass awareness, but digital is overtaking for conversion.
